1.authors: Guo L, Fan XY, Qiao X, Montell C, Huang J
1.title: An octopamine receptor confers selective toxicity of amitraz on honeybees and Varroa mites
1.note: Verified via PMC full text, PubMed, and CrossRef (all three agree). Confirms the candidate PMC8313232 identifier: the paper shows Octbeta2R is the sole in vivo target of amitraz and that three specific residues in the receptor's binding pocket account for the differential (honeybee-vs-Varroa-mite) sensitivity. Note the selectivity axis in the paper is honeybee-vs-mite (pollinator safety), not explicitly tick-vs-vertebrate, but the mechanism (small number of octopamine-receptor binding-site residues driving amitraz selectivity) matches the requested reference exactly. This is the correct paper for PMC8313232 -- description in the task brief was accurate.

2.authors: Cole LM, Nicholson RA, Casida JE
2.title: Action of phenylpyrazole insecticides at the GABA-gated chloride channel
2.note: DOI and full bibliographic details confirmed via CrossRef API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1006/PEST.1993.1035) and corroborating ScienceDirect/NPIC/ADS listings. This is the classic paper establishing that phenylpyrazoles (fipronil's chemical class) act at the insect GABA-gated chloride channel (RDL). No PMID: a PubMed search for this title/authors returned zero results -- Pesticide Biochemistry and Physiology from 1993 does not appear to be PubMed-indexed for this article. DOI-based citation is solid; do not fabricate a PMID.

3.authors: Chen L, Durkin KA, Casida JE
3.title: Structural model for gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor noncompetitive antagonist binding: widely diverse structures fit the same site
3.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA 103(13):5185-5190
3.note: Verified via PubMed and PNAS record. Confirms fipronil (and other noncompetitive antagonists) bind within the chloride-channel pore lined by the five M2 transmembrane segments, at a site formed by residues contributed by all five subunits (i.e., the pore-lining/inter-subunit interface of the pentamer) -- key residues identified near A2', T6', L9' of M2. The paper frames this as a single pore-lumen site rather than explicitly using the term 'inter-subunit'; that framing is my inference from the M2-pentamer geometry described, not a verbatim quote -- flag this nuance if precision on 'inter-subunit' phrasing matters for the manuscript.

4.title: Principles of activation and permeation in an anion-selective Cys-loop receptor
4.note: Verified via PubMed. This is the Hibbs & Gouaux 2011 Nature paper requested -- crystal structure of the C. elegans glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluCl) in complex with ivermectin (PDB 3RHW/3RIF), glutamate, and picrotoxin. Ivermectin binds at the transmembrane-domain interface between adjacent subunits, distinct from the glutamate orthosteric site. Actual title differs slightly from the commonly paraphrased 'GluCl structure with ivermectin' description but is the same paper/PMID/DOI.

5.title: Neonicotinoid insecticide toxicology: mechanisms of selective action
5.venue: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology 45:247-268
5.note: Verified via PubMed. Standard, highly cited review establishing neonicotinoids' selective action at insect vs. vertebrate nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChR).

6.title: Mechanism of action of organophosphorus and carbamate insecticides
6.note: Verified via PubMed. Standard reference for OP/carbamate inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE).

7.authors: Panchenko AR, Kondrashov F, Bryant S
7.title: Prediction of functional sites by analysis of sequence and structure conservation
7.note: Verified via PubMed. Abstract/method supports that well-conserved, spatially clustered residues (functional/binding sites) stand out against lower background sequence conservation, i.e. functional-site conservation exceeds whole-protein average. An alternative candidate, Bartlett GJ, Porter CT, Borkakoti N, Thornton JM (2002) 'Analysis of catalytic residues in enzyme active sites', J Mol Biol 324(1):105-121, doi:10.1016/s0022-2836(02)01036-7, PMID 12421562, was also verified (same rigor) but its abstract does not explicitly state the comparative conservation claim, only that catalytic residues were analyzed for conservation among other properties -- Panchenko et al. is the better direct fit and is listed as primary; Bartlett et al. 2002 is a solid secondary/alternative citation if a second reference is wanted.

8.authors: Wilson CJ, Choy WY, Karttunen M
8.title: AlphaFold2: A Role for Disordered Protein/Region Prediction?
8.note: Verified via PubMed. Directly supports the claim: finds AlphaFold2's pLDDT confidence score is 'an excellent measure of residue-wise disorder' -- i.e. low pLDDT correlates with intrinsic disorder. This is the best direct match among the candidates offered; Akdel et al. 2022 Nat Struct Mol Biol and Ruff & Pappu 2021 J Mol Biol were not separately verified since Wilson/Choy/Karttunen already gives a clean, direct citation for this specific claim.

9.authors: Chmelar J, Kotal J, Langhansova H, Kotsyfakis M
9.title: Protease Inhibitors in Tick Saliva: The Role of Serpins and Cystatins in Tick-host-Pathogen Interaction
9.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology 7:216
9.note: Verified via PMC full text and PubMed. Review confirms tick salivary cystatins (e.g. sialostatin L, sialostatin L2) act as tight-binding reversible protein-protein-interaction inhibitors of host cysteine proteases (cathepsins), immunomodulating via direct protein engagement rather than via a classical small-molecule-druggable active-site pocket.

10.authors: Gassel M, Wolf C, Noack S, Williams H, Ilg T
10.title: The novel isoxazoline ectoparasiticide fluralaner: selective inhibition of arthropod gamma-aminobutyric acid- and L-glutamate-gated chloride channels and insecticidal/acaricidal activity
10.note: Verified via PubMed. Confirms fluralaner potently and selectively blocks arthropod GABA-gated and L-glutamate-gated chloride channels, more potent than picrotoxinin/dieldrin, with acaricidal activity against cattle ticks.
